newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC urges swift end to C4 funding formula.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC urges swift end to C4 funding formula.

text.p: Britain's Independent Television Commission (ITC) watchdog on Tuesday urged the government to phase out the Channel 4 (C4) funding formula by the end of next year.

"We believe that the funding formula should have a single transition year in 1998 beyond which there should be no further payments," the ITC said in a letter to National Heritage Secretary Chris Smith. Designed as a system of income support for state-owned C4, the success of the channel has meant that the ITV commercial television companies have been receiving hefty annual payments from C4.

The ITV companies receive 50 percent of the surplus when C4's share of terrestrial TV advertising and sponsorship income tops 14 percent. They are obliged to subsidise C4 should its income drop below that level.

C4 handed over 87 million pounds ($145 million) to the ITV companies last year, taking the total over four years to 257 million pounds. The Labour government is taking soundings on the formula before deciding its fate.

The ITC said only 35 percent of the surplus should go to ITV companies in 1998 before it was eliminated from 1999. If not totally eliminated in 1999, the payment should not exceed 10 percent, the ITC added.
The ITC suggested that 1998 should be seen as a "transitional" year as ITV companies would still be liable to pay annual licence fees at existing rates.
The licences, which began in 1993, run for 10 years but companies can seek early renewal and a number see this as a chance to push for lower annual payments.
The ITC said extra funds retained by C4 should be invested on programmes which would develop its remit to cater for minority interests and tastes.
It said the phasing out of the formula would also allow more resources to be allocated to the digital terrestrial television frequencies jointly awarded to C4 and the ITV network.
